task.goal: Stop malformed API requests from causing crashes while preserving the public response contract.
task.context: A Node service accepts JSON requests through three HTTP handlers. Current failures include uncaught validation exceptions, inconsistent 400 responses, and one oversized-body path.

constraints.text: Do not change successful response shapes or status codes for valid requests
Do not remove payload limits or expose stack traces to clients
Keep the change within the HTTP boundary and shared validation code

success.text: Malformed and oversized requests return a consistent documented 400 or 413 response
The existing valid-request contract tests remain green
A bounded malformed-input suite produces no uncaught 5xx responses

candidates.title: Centralize validation at the HTTP boundary
candidates.summary: Validate each request with the existing schema and map failures to one safe error contract.
candidates.mechanism: Add a small middleware wrapper around the three handlers, preserve successful values, classify schema and size failures, and emit a sanitized error body with a request ID.
assumptions: The existing schemas cover the required fields
risks: A handler may depend on an undocumented coercion
validation: Assert no stack trace is returned

candidates.title: Wrap each handler in a local try/catch
candidates.summary: Convert thrown validation errors into 400 responses at each route.
candidates.mechanism: Add repeated try/catch blocks to the three handlers and return a common error helper when parsing fails.
assumptions: All malformed input failures are thrown synchronously
risks: One route can drift from the others
Unexpected programming errors may be hidden

candidates.title: Coerce all request fields before validation
candidates.summary: Convert values to strings or defaults to reduce validation failures.
candidates.mechanism: Normalize every incoming field and accept values that the current schema rejects.
risks: Invalid data can pass the boundary

candidates.title: Increase the request body limit
candidates.summary: Avoid oversized-body errors by allowing larger payloads.
candidates.mechanism: Raise the global body parser limit and leave route validation unchanged.
risks: Memory pressure and denial-of-service exposure increase
Does not fix uncaught validation failures
validation: Send a larger request through one handler

candidates.title: Replace the HTTP validation layer
candidates.summary: Move all handlers to a new framework with built-in validation.
candidates.mechanism: Rewrite the server adapter and route definitions, then port the existing handlers.
assumptions: A framework migration can be isolated

candidates.title: Add malformed-input fuzz tests only
candidates.summary: Improve detection without changing the request boundary.
candidates.mechanism: Generate malformed JSON and field combinations against the current handlers and record failures.
risks: The current production crash path remains
